exempt.src/services/tracked-response.ts:tracked: UNREVIEWED. THIS IS A FINDING, and the most serious one in this file. Both scans here (src/services/tracked-response.ts:268 reactive, :282 the ten-minute reconciler started at src/server-bootstrap/routes-loader.ts:737) walk listAllMemory with prefix tracked-response. across EVERY namespace and evaluate whatever they find, whoever wrote it. The contract's own value then supplies all three of: the key to read, which readWatchedValue (:119) fetches with listAllMemory by exact key with NO visibility and NO ownership check, so any record on the node is reachable; the field of that value to splice into the message body (injectResult, :128); and the senderGhii and recipientGhii handed to sendDirectMessage (src/services/message-send.ts:122), which takes the sender on trust because authorisation lives at each door and this path has none. A principal holding plain memory:write can therefore write tracked-response.{id}.latest into a namespace it already controls and make the node read any owner's memory record by key and deliver it as a direct message that appears to come from any account. tracked-response. is not in RESERVED_OWNER_KEY_PREFIXES (src/utils/reserved-keys.ts:61). The fix is a code change in files this unit does not own: bind the scan and the watched-key read to the contract's own ownerGaii, and make the sender the record's namespace rather than a field of its value.
